source: knowledge/DEMO-SCRIPT.md section 1 (the six shots at a glance), section 3 (S1 to S6, second by second) and the S5 and S6 sub-shot paragraphs. The numbers are the document's own steps, read back through the 60 step a second clock, so a row here and a row there cannot drift without the validator saying so.
why: One command plays one documented take: this file is the shot table as data. tools/play_demo.py reads a table by name, plays the script the table names, and then asks the game's own log whether each shot's line was written. Card t_fb7e8271 made the file; card t_866814e6 made `full` the 180 s take the card asks for and kept the 253.5 s three fight take as full-three.

narration.note: The recorder draws no text on the frame and writes no narrator line into the video: the shots are the game's own pixels, and the captions DEMO-SCRIPT.md names belong to the edit (R44), not to this take. A table row that carries a narrator, narration or voiceover field is refused by the validator, so the take cannot grow a voice over quietly.

full.why: The three battle take, Morgan at the gate, the deck watch and Percy in his office, 253.5 s: the full route and the QA take since Nayil's order (manager decision 2026-11-01: exactly three battles, every fight ends by spare or 0 HP). The 180 s take of card t_866814e6, built around a deck hound fight and a forced defeat, is retired. The tooling needs every table's shots to meet end to end from step 0, so a 180 s highlights table cannot be a subset of this take; that recut is left to the demo card with data/demo/run_002.json as its source.

talk-win.name: talk-win
talk-win.title: the S6 talking win alone: the deck, TALK three times, SPARE, the ship's log save
talk-win.clock_note: One take, one launch, one deck. 134.33 s is 8,060 steps at 60 a second. The fight rows are driven by the game's own log lines, so a press cannot land on a board or a dodge: each one names the line it waits on and carries the fallback step the run uses if the log is block buffered.
talk-win.why: Card t_e48b13a6: the talking win as a path the demo harness can select by name, without the 180 s take around it and without a person at the keyboard. It is the same fight and the same save the submission take uses, started on the deck through PP_ROUTE_HOLD=drive.

command-win.name: command-win
command-win.title: the S6 single command win: the deck, the hound ended by ONE FIGHT, the ship's log save
command-win.clock_note: One take, one launch, one deck. 129.33 s is 7,760 steps at 60 a second. The Deck Watch is cleared first because the deck is a corridor: its trigger at (4,7) sits west of the hound's at (6,7), so no walk reaches the hound without passing it. The hound then falls to one Confirm on FIGHT, because it carries 2 hp and 2 is the floor of the game's own damage.
command-win.why: Card t_e48b13a6: the single command win as a path the demo harness can select by name. The win it proves is the hound's, the only fight on the deck a single command can end.
